hints.title: Subject Diversity Aggregation
hints.text: Aggregate study records per student to count unique subjects explored.

hints.title: Threshold Filtering
hints.text: Filter for scholars who have engaged with at least three distinct academic subjects.

hints.title: Total Effort Sorting
hints.text: Sum the total study hours accumulated and sort in descending order of effort.

hints.title: Reference Implementation
hints.text:
```sql
WITH student_stats AS (
    SELECT 
        s.student_id,
        st.student_name,
        st.major,
        COUNT(DISTINCT s.subject) AS distinct_subjects,
        SUM(s.hours_spent) AS total_study_hours
    FROM study_sessions s
    JOIN students st ON s.student_id = st.student_id
    GROUP BY s.student_id, st.student_name, st.major
)
SELECT 
    student_id,
    student_name,
    major,
    ROUND(total_study_hours, 2) AS total_study_hours
FROM student_stats
WHERE distinct_subjects >= 3
ORDER BY total_study_hours DESC, student_id ASC;
```

complexity.notes: Group aggregation by student followed by count filtering and sorting.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Correlated subqueries per student recalculate distinct counts inefficiently.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Single group-by aggregation evaluates hours and subjects concurrently.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Use group aggregation with COUNT(DISTINCT) and HAVING filters.

import pandas as pd

def find_students_with_study_spiral_pattern(students: pd.DataFrame, study_sessions: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    grouped = study_sessions.groupby('student_id').agg(
        distinct_subjects=('subject', 'nunique'),
        total_study_hours=('hours_spent', 'sum')
    ).reset_index()
    
    valid = grouped[grouped['distinct_subjects'] >= 3].copy()
    valid['total_study_hours'] = valid['total_study_hours'].round(2)
    
    res = valid.merge(students, on='student_id', how='inner')
    res = res.sort_values(by=['total_study_hours', 'student_id'], ascending=[False, True])
    return res[['student_id', 'student_name', 'major', 'total_study_hours']]
